name: ISERROR
description: ISERROR returns TRUE if the supplied value is any Excel error (#N/A, #VALUE!, #REF!, #DIV/0!, #NUM!, #NAME?, or #NULL!), and FALSE otherwise.
tldr: Tests whether a value is any error.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value, cell reference, or formula result to test.

advancedExamples.title: Test a cell that holds an error
advancedExamples.scenario: A1 contains #N/A from a failed lookup.
advancedExamples.description: Detect any error in a cell
advancedExamples.explanation: #N/A is an error, so ISERROR returns TRUE.

advancedExamples.title: Branch on error safely
advancedExamples.scenario: Show a fallback when a calculation fails.
advancedExamples.description: Combine with IF to replace errors
advancedExamples.explanation: If B1 is 0 the division errors and ISERROR returns TRUE, triggering the fallback.

howItWorks: ISERROR returns TRUE when the value is any of the seven Excel error values, and FALSE for normal values. It is broader than ISNA (which catches only #N/A) and ISERR (which catches all errors except #N/A). To learn which error occurred, use ERROR.TYPE.

howToSteps.name: Pick the value
howToSteps.text: Select the cell or formula result to test.

howToSteps.name: Use with IF
howToSteps.text: Wrap it in IF to provide a fallback for errors.

limitations: Catches all errors including #N/A; use ISNA if #N/A is meaningful and should be left alone.
Does not identify which error occurred; use ERROR.TYPE for that.
Returns FALSE for ordinary values (not an error).

commonErrors.cause: ISERROR treats #N/A like any other error.
commonErrors.fix: Use ISNA or IFNA when #N/A should be handled differently.
Use IFERROR, which evaluates the expression once.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ISERROR works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax and behavior.

faq.question: ISERROR vs ISERR?
faq.answer: ISERR is the same except it ignores #N/A; ISERROR includes #N/A.

faq.question: How do I get the error code?
faq.answer: Use ERROR.TYPE on the error cell to get a numeric code.

faq.question: What is the simplest way to replace errors?
faq.answer: IFERROR replaces any error with a fallback in a single step.
